definition: A person who has memorized enough corporate code, Diaspora terms-of-service clauses, and municipal ordinance to navigate legal confrontations without formal training or credentials. Respected in Tier 2-3 communities as a resource; viewed with contempt by actual legal professionals; occasionally recruited by firms who need deniable procedural expertise.
origin: Street cant originating in the Lakeshore district where informal legal aid networks developed in response to unaffordable formal counsel
usage: Used throughout Old Harbor and Lakeshore communities; used dismissively by Spire legal professionals
example: Don't sign anything before you talk to Mireille — she's the best lakeshore lawyer in this block cluster and she's beaten Axiom compliance officers twice.
